author: shsam
comment:
These RQs need to be rephrased  in a scientific way.
Currently it feels like only an engineering problem than a research problem.

The main issue is that the current RQs are phrased around what to build (“extend,” “normalize,” “place notebooks into categories”), rather than what scientific phenomenon you want to investigate.

A more scientific formulation

RQ1 — Cross-platform reproducibility infrastructure

RQ1: To what extent can a platform-independent reproducibility workflow support the analysis of computational notebooks across heterogeneous research platforms?

This changes the focus from “How do we add Codeberg and Zenodo connectors?” to the more research-oriented question of whether platform-independent processing can generalize across repositories.

RQ2 — Metadata heterogeneity and integration

RQ2: How does metadata heterogeneity across research platforms affect the integration and representation of computational notebooks and their reproducibility-related information?

RQ3: To what extent can rule-based and AI-based approaches reliably characterize computational notebooks into reproducibility-relevant categories, and how do their classifications compare with human judgments?

RQ4: To what extent do computational notebooks differ across corss-platforms with respect to metadata completeness, execution outcomes, failure causes, and reproducibility-relevant categories?



You can then refer to research questions in other chapters to show how ach RQs were addressed.
